chunks: We said: There is no choice in that,

because a person who doubts the Imamate of Ibn Hasan (peace be upon him) must have discourse with him regarding the explicit narration of his Imamate and be occupied with providing proofs for it. It is not permissible, while doubting it, to speak about the reason for the occultation, because discourse on the offshoots is not valid except after the fundamentals are established for them, just as it is not permissible to speak about the reason for the harm to children before the wisdom of the Ancient One (God) is established and that He does not do the ugly. We preferred discourse on his Imamate (peace be upon him) over discourse on his occultation and its reason, because discourse on his Imamate is based on intellectual matters that do not admit doubt.
ai.seo_question: Why should the proof of Imamate be established before discussing the reason for occultation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the jurisprudential principle of 'usul vs. furū' to argue that the rational certainty of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari’s Imamate must be established before addressing the speculative wisdom of his occultation. This mirrors the theological approach of discussing divine attributes before their effects, ensuring that the foundation of belief is secure before exploring the mysteries of the unseen.
